label: ai-generated
title: Why we put things off
text:
Most of us have, at some point, left an unpleasant task until the last possible moment. For a long time, procrastination was [[1]] down to simple laziness or poor time management. More recent research, however, has [[2]] to light a rather different explanation: the habit has more to do with emotions than with discipline. When a task makes us anxious or bored, delaying it brings instant relief, and our brains are highly [[3]] to that kind of short-term reward. [[4]] this, the strategy is self-defeating: the task does not go away, and the stress [[5]] up as the deadline approaches.

One technique that psychologists recommend is to [[6]] a deliberately tiny first step, so small that starting feels almost effortless. Another is, surprisingly, to be kinder to yourself. In one study, students who [[7]] themselves for procrastinating before a first exam were less likely to delay again before the next. Harsh self-criticism, it seems, only makes the task more threatening, and [[8]] strengthens the urge to avoid it.

explanation.en: 'Put something down to' means 'explain it as caused by': 'was put down to simple laziness'. 'Brought down' means 'reduced' and 'laid down' means 'established as a rule'.
explanation.cs: 'Put sth down to sth' = připisovat něco něčemu. 'Bring down' znamená snížit a 'lay down' stanovit pravidlo, takže význam nesedí.

explanation.en: 'Bring something to light' means 'reveal it', and here it has an object: 'has brought to light a different explanation'. 'Come to light' is also a real phrase, but it has no object, so it cannot take 'a rather different explanation'.
explanation.cs: 'Bring sth to light' = odhalit něco (má předmět). 'Come to light' také existuje, ale je bez předmětu (vyjít najevo), proto zde nesedí.

explanation.en: After the gap comes 'to that kind of reward', and only 'sensitive' takes 'to'. 'Aware', 'conscious' and 'fond' are all followed by 'of'.
explanation.cs: Za mezerou je 'to', a s 'to' se pojí jen 'sensitive to' (citlivý na). 'Aware', 'conscious' i 'fond' vyžadují 'of'.

explanation.en: The gap is followed by a noun phrase, 'this', and then a comma, so a preposition of contrast is needed: 'Despite this'. 'Although' needs a full clause, and 'However' or 'Nevertheless' would need to stand alone before the comma.
explanation.cs: Za mezerou je jen 'this' (podstatné jméno), takže potřebujeme předložku 'Despite'. 'Although' chce celou větu a 'However' či 'Nevertheless' by stály samostatně bez 'this'.

explanation.en: 'Build up' means 'increase gradually', which suits stress growing 'as the deadline approaches'. 'Rise up' means 'rebel', and 'swell up' is used for parts of the body.
explanation.cs: 'Build up' = postupně narůstat. 'Rise up' znamená povstat (vzbouřit se) a 'swell up' se říká např. o oteklém kotníku.

explanation.en: The collocation is 'take a step': 'take a deliberately tiny first step'. 'Make' is a common mistake here, because Czech speakers translate 'udělat krok'.
explanation.cs: Anglicky se krok 'bere': 'take a step'. Čeština říká 'udělat krok', proto láká 'make' nebo 'do', ale ty se s 'step' nepojí.

explanation.en: All four verbs can take 'themselves for', but the text recommends being 'kinder to yourself' and warns against 'harsh self-criticism', so only 'forgave' fits. 'Blamed' is the opposite of the idea the paragraph supports.
explanation.cs: Všechna slovesa gramaticky sedí s 'themselves for', ale rozhoduje kontext: text doporučuje být k sobě laskavější. 'Blamed' (obviňovali se) je přesný opak.

explanation.en: 'Thereby' means 'as a result of this' and can stand before a verb: 'and thereby strengthens the urge'. 'Whereby', 'wherein' and 'whereupon' introduce relative clauses and cannot follow 'and' like this.
explanation.cs: 'Thereby' = tím (čímž) a může stát přímo před slovesem. 'Whereby', 'wherein' a 'whereupon' uvozují vztažnou větu a po 'and' takto stát nemohou.
